bearing.resolver.v1alpha1.OrderingKey.sc.description:
OrderingKey is the key every write is compared by, left to right:
 (observed_at, observation_id, event_id, content_hash)
 (docs/spec/data-model.md, "Ordering and idempotency"). The strings compare
 by their UTF-8 bytes; pkg/model compares keys.

^(contentHash)$.description:
Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the JCS form of the observation's data; for a
 manual event, of the payload.

^(eventId)$.description: The event that carried it, which includes the source.

^(observationId)$.description: The observation that made the write; for a manual event, the event ID.

content_hash.description:
Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the JCS form of the observation's data; for a
 manual event, of the payload.

event_id.description: The event that carried it, which includes the source.

observation_id.description: The observation that made the write; for a manual event, the event ID.

bearing.resolver.v1alpha1.ScopeWatermark.description:
The `wm/` entries keep a scope's watermarks apart, so that a sync adds one
 small entry and rewrites none that grows. The entry at the scope's key is
 its head. A head written before issue #136 holds every watermark in
 `watermarks` and has `bucketed` unset; the first sync to change them moves
 them into entries of their own. A bucketed head holds no watermarks: they
 are in the entries at the head's key plus "/" and a bucket number, each a
 ScopeWatermarks that holds, sorted by key, the watermarks whose key's
 observed_at falls in that quarter hour of the epoch (the bucket). A late
 claim finds the first watermark with a greater key by reading its bucket
 and the ones after it inside the head's blocks, so an entry is only ever read by
 its key. A bucket is written when it gains or loses a watermark. A binary
 from before the buckets reads a bucketed head as having no watermarks; the
 format is unreleased, so nothing guards against it.

^(lastBucket)$.description:
In a bucketed head, the highest bucket that held a watermark, which is in
 the last block, so a lookup past the latest watermark reads nothing. It
 may stay after that watermark is gone.

blocks.description:
In a bucketed head, the blocks of 1,024 buckets (block n covers buckets
 1024n to 1024n+1023) that can hold a watermark of the scope itself, in
 increasing order. A lookup reads buckets only inside them, so a gap of
 years between watermarks costs no reads. A block may stay after its last
 watermark is gone.

bucketed.description: Set in a head whose watermarks are in buckets' entries.

last_bucket.description:
In a bucketed head, the highest bucket that held a watermark, which is in
 the last block, so a lookup past the latest watermark reads nothing. It
 may stay after that watermark is gone.

linked.description:
In a head, the keys of the heads of the scopes of subjects merged into
 this one's subject, whose watermarks also apply here. They are left where
 they are, not copied.

watermarks.description: The watermarks, in a head that is not bucketed and in a bucket's entry.

bearing.resolver.v1alpha1.ScopeWatermark.title:
ScopeWatermarks is the watermarks of a scope (source, subject, direction and
 predicate, or the subject's identity evidence in a namespace), sorted by
 `at`. A watermark is dropped once another with an earlier or equal `at` has
 a greater or equal key, so the rest rise together: in order of key they are
 in order of `at`.

bearing.resolver.v1alpha1.Watermark.sche.description:
Watermark ends, from valid time `at` on and with `key`, every fact of the
 source in its scope that the observation did not claim, including facts
 whose claims are applied later (docs/spec/data-model.md, "Snapshot
 scopes").

at.description: Start of the ending in valid time.

reason.description: SNAPSHOT for a scope, DELETED for entity.deleted.
reason.title: Support Reason

bearing.resolver.v1alpha1.Watermark.sche.title: Watermark
